title: Jeonbuk education office school bus system leak exposes student addresses and bus routes
date_note: Date the office posted its notice, as reported by Dailysecu (published 20 Nov); the Ministry of Education Cyber Safety Center told the office of a suspected leak on 15 Nov.
geo_basis: headquarters (province education office, Jeonju); no victim city stated
summary: Dailysecu reports that the Jeonbuk Teachers' Federation, in a 19 November statement, demanded disclosure of the scale and cause of a leak from the Jeonbuk Provincial Office of Education's school bus management system. The office listed eight items, including student name, address, parent contact and bus route, after a 15 November notice from the Cyber Safety Center. Media reported about 10,000 records; the office has not confirmed a final number.
plain: A teachers' group in South Korea says student addresses, parent contacts and school bus routes leaked from a provincial education office system. The number of records is not confirmed.
exec: Student addresses and bus routes leaked from a school system; the office has not confirmed the scale, and the teachers' group says schools' notices differ.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Affected families should follow the education office's notice.
impact: Eight items listed by the office: school name, student name, grade, class, student address, parent contact, bus plate number and route.

validation.note: Only Dailysecu read; the office's own notice and the union statement were not read directly. Record count is media-reported (about 10,000), not confirmed by the office.

review.note: Dailysecu 20 Nov: 15 Nov Cyber Safety Center notice, 17 Nov office notice, 8 items, about 10,000 media-reported, union statement 19 Nov, scale unconfirmed
